title: How to Get Repeat Customers When Selling Online in Pakistan
summary: How to get repeat customers when selling online in Pakistan: the customer list to keep, the follow-up messages that work, and what kills repeat orders.
body_markdown:
Repeat customers come from three things: the parcel arrived the way you described it, somebody answered quickly when there was a problem, and you contacted the buyer again before they forgot your page. Loyalty cards and standing discounts are far down that list.


Most resellers in Pakistan sell to a person once and never speak to them again. The order closes in WhatsApp, the chat scrolls away, and next month starts from zero. Everything spent winning that customer — the boosted post, the twenty replies you typed, the hours — gets thrown away after one sale.


The fix is a habit, not a tool:


- **Save every buyer** on the day their parcel is delivered.
- **Message once after delivery** to check the product reached them fine.
- **Come back with something new** , not with a discount.
- **Fix complaints fast** — a problem handled well sells again.


Here is how each piece works for a cash-on-delivery seller.


## Why the second order is the cheapest one you will get


Every first sale carries a cost. The ad, the price-checkers who asked and vanished, the half hour of replies. A repeat buyer skips all of it. They know the page, they know the parcel turns up, and they usually order faster and argue less about delivery charges.


Repeat buyers also refuse fewer parcels. Someone who has already handed you cash at their door is far more likely to accept the next one, and in Pakistan that matters more than almost anywhere, because a refused COD parcel costs you the delivery in both directions. If refused parcels are your main leak, read[how to reduce COD returns (RTO)](https://www.markaz.app/blog-post/reduce-cod-returns-pakistan) next to this guide, and[COD return rates in Pakistan](https://www.markaz.app/blog-post/cod-return-rates-in-pakistan-how-to-reduce-them) to work out what yours actually is.


They also bring people. Reseller pages that grow without ad money almost always grow on one thing: a satisfied customer forwarding your number to a cousin, a colleague or a WhatsApp group.


## Repeat business starts before the follow-up message


No message brings back a customer who opened the parcel and found something other than what they saw in the photo. Before any retention trick, three things have to hold.


- **The product is what you showed.** Colour, size, material, quantity, all of it.
- **Delivery lands inside the window you promised.** Quote the real window, not the best case.
- **Somebody replies.** A message left until tomorrow is usually a customer you have already lost.


Say it plainly in the chat before the order is confirmed: what is in the parcel, what the buyer pays at the door, and how many days it takes. Orders you place on Markaz inside Pakistan usually reach the customer in three to five days, and orders from[Markaz China](https://www.markaz.app/china) in ten to seventeen, so quote the window you can keep and let the parcel beat it. The rest of that groundwork is in[how to build customer trust when selling online in Pakistan](https://www.markaz.app/blog-post/how-to-build-customer-trust-when-selling-online-in-pakistan) .


## Build a customer list you actually own


Followers are not a customer list. Instagram decides who sees your post, and a page that reached 3,000 people last month may reach 300 this month. A phone number saved in your own file is yours either way.


### What to save, the day the parcel is delivered


- **Name and number.** The number they ordered from, not the one in the delivery slip if they differ.
- **City or area.** It tells you where your deliveries succeed and what sells where.
- **What they bought** — including the size, colour or variant.
- **The delivery date.** This is what you count days from later.
- **One line of context.** "Wanted black, took brown." "Bought for her sister's mehndi." "Asked if you have kids' sizes."


A notebook works. A free spreadsheet on your phone works better because you can sort it by product and by date. The tool matters less than doing it the same day — a week later you will not remember which Ayesha bought the trimmer.


### Save the contact, not just the chat


Save the number to your phone properly, and ask the customer to save yours. That one step decides whether your WhatsApp status and any broadcast you send ever reach them, because WhatsApp only delivers a broadcast to people who have your number saved. If you send anything to more than a handful of buyers,[using WhatsApp Broadcast for your business](https://www.markaz.app/blog-post/whatsapp-broadcast) explains the setup.


Keep two lists: people who bought, and people who asked but did not. The second list is for new stock; the first is for everything.


## The three messages that bring people back


You do not need a campaign calendar. You need three messages, sent to the right person at the right time.


### 1. The delivery check, a day or two after it arrives


Short, no selling:


*"Assalam-o-alaikum. Your parcel was delivered on Tuesday — did everything reach you fine? If there is any issue with it, tell me today and I will sort it out."*


This message catches a problem while you can still fix it, proves a person is behind the page, and is the natural moment to ask for a photo you can post. Do not attach an offer to it. The one time you contact a customer purely to help them is the one that earns the next order.


### 2. The new-arrival message, when you have something they would want


This is where the notes column pays off. Someone who bought a kitchen organiser hears from you when kitchen stock lands, not when phone covers do. Sending everything to everybody is how people mute you.


*"You took the fan from me in June — the same brand's heater just came in and I have three. Want me to keep one?"*


Naming the earlier order is the whole trick. It tells them you remember, and it makes the message read like a person rather than a forward.


### 3. The reorder nudge, for anything that runs out or gets outgrown


Skincare, supplements, socks, kids' clothes, detergent, phone accessories that break — all of these have a natural second order. Work out roughly how long the product lasts, then message a little before it runs out.


*"That serum you ordered should be finishing around now — want me to send another before the stock goes?"*


Three rules for all three messages. Write to the person, never as a visible group. Send once and stop; chasing turns a warm buyer into a blocked contact. And never open with "Dear customer" — every forwarded advert in Pakistan opens that way, and people delete on sight.


## Give people a reason to return that is not a discount


A standing discount teaches customers to wait for the discount, and it comes straight out of the margin you were going to live on. Better reasons to come back:


- **New stock first.** Message your past buyers before you post publicly. It makes them feel early rather than marketed at.
- **The bundle.** The thing they bought plus the obvious companion — case with the trimmer, filters with the bottle — at a price slightly better than two separate orders.
- **A small extra in the parcel.** Not a discount, a surprise. It costs little and it is what people photograph.
- **Being the person who finds things.** When a customer asks for something you do not stock, go and find it. That is the habit that turns a page into a shop people come back to by default.


New stock is the strongest of these, and it is the easiest to arrange. Pull fresh products from the[Markaz Shop categories](https://www.markaz.app/shop/categories) and check the[current deals](https://www.markaz.app/shop/deals) before you message anyone, so you have something real to offer. Because Markaz has no minimum order, you can test one unit of a product on your existing buyers before you commit to selling it widely.


## The parcel is your shop — use it


Your customer never sees a shopfront. They see a courier bag on their doorstep, and that is the only physical contact your business has with them.


Put a small card in every parcel: your page name, your WhatsApp number, one line inviting them to message you a photo of the product in use, and what to do if something is wrong. Handwriting the customer's name on it takes ten seconds and is remembered far longer than it should be.


Also make sure the parcel survives the journey — a product that arrives scratched cancels every follow-up message you were planning to send.[Packaging and branding for small online sellers in Pakistan](https://www.markaz.app/blog-post/packaging-branding-for-small-online-sellers-in-pakistan) covers what to buy and what a COD parcel actually has to survive.


## A complaint handled well sells again


The customer who complains is still talking to you. The one who is disappointed and says nothing is already gone. Most sellers waste that chance by going quiet. What works, in order:


1. **Reply fast, even if you have no answer yet.** "I have seen this, give me till the evening and I will tell you exactly what I can do" beats silence while you figure it out.
2. **Apologise once, then move to the fix.** Long apologies read as excuses.
3. **Say what happens next and when.** Uncertainty is what makes people post about you.
4. **Follow up after it is resolved.** This is the message people remember.


Selling on Markaz helps here, because returns run through the platform's 7-day return window and buyer protection rather than leaving you personally out of pocket for a product you never touched. That is what lets you say yes quickly to a genuine complaint.[Customer satisfaction for small businesses](https://www.markaz.app/blog-post/customer-satisfaction) goes further into the service side.


## Sell more than one thing to the same buyer


Most resellers cap their own repeat rate by selling one narrow category. If everything you carry is phone covers, a customer needs a new phone before they need you again.


The people who build steady repeat business carry a small spread: something for the house, something for kids, something personal. They still lead with one category, but they can say yes when a buyer asks for something else. Working through the[Markaz dropshipping portal](https://www.markaz.app/dropshipping-portal) , adding a category costs nothing up front — you list it, and you only order after the customer has bought.


If you are still choosing where to sell all of this,[the top platforms for selling online in Pakistan](https://www.markaz.app/blog-post/platforms-for-selling-online) compares the options, and[COD dropshipping in Pakistan](https://www.markaz.app/blog-post/cod-dropshipping-in-pakistan) covers the mechanics end to end. For the wider picture of what sells and what goes wrong,[selling online in Pakistan](https://www.markaz.app/blog-post/selling-online-in-pakistan) covers the benefits and the challenges.


## A weekly routine that takes about an hour


Retention fails because it is nobody's job. Put it on one day of the week and it survives.


1. **Add last week's buyers to the list.** Name, number, area, product, date, one note.
2. **Send delivery checks** to everyone whose parcel landed in the last few days.
3. **Pick one group and message them.** Twenty past buyers of one category, one relevant product.
4. **Chase the reorder window.** Anyone who bought something consumable a month or two ago.
5. **Save what worked.** Which message got replies, which product people asked about next.


Twenty messages that name the person beat two hundred that do not.


## Know whether it is working


Two numbers are enough, and you can get both out of the list you are already keeping.


- **Repeat rate:** of the orders you delivered this month, how many came from someone who had bought before.
- **Days between orders:** for buyers who came back, how long the gap was. It tells you when to send the reorder message.


**Worked example (illustrative numbers, not Markaz data):** you deliver 100 orders in a month and 18 of them are from people already in your list — an 18% repeat rate. If those 18 orders came an average of five weeks after the previous one, then four weeks is when your reorder message should go out, not three months later when they have found somebody else.


Watch the direction, not the number. A repeat rate that climbs slowly month after month is a business getting sturdier, whatever it started at.


## What stops people coming back


- **Over-promising delivery.** Two days quoted, six days delivered. The product can be perfect and the customer still will not order again.
- **Answering late.** In COD selling, a slow reply is a cancelled order and a lost customer in one.
- **Broadcasting the same message to everybody.** Fast way to get muted.
- **Discounting by default.** You train people to wait, and you lose the margin that pays for the next order.
- **Going quiet when something goes wrong.** The single biggest destroyer of repeat business on Pakistani reseller pages.
- **Never saving the number.** No list, no second order, no matter how good the product was.


## Frequently asked questions


### How soon should I message a customer after delivery?


One to two days after the parcel lands. Sooner and they may not have opened it; much later and any problem has already turned into resentment. Keep it short, ask whether it arrived fine, and do not sell anything in that message.


### Do I need an app or a loyalty programme for this?


No. A phone contact list and a spreadsheet cover everything in this guide. Points and loyalty schemes are for shops with thousands of customers; for a reseller with a few hundred buyers, a message that names the person and their last order does more.


### How often can I message past customers without annoying them?


As a rough guide, once or twice a month unless there is a real reason — a restock they asked about, or a product that matches what they bought. Relevance matters more than frequency. A monthly forward to everyone gets muted faster than two targeted messages a week.


### Should I offer a discount to bring someone back?


Use it as a one-off, not a policy. A small discount for a customer whose delivery was late is good service. A standing "10% for old customers" trains people to wait for it and eats the margin you need. New stock and bundles bring people back without costing you the same.


### What if my product is something people only buy once?


Then the repeat order has to come from a different product, which is the argument for carrying more than one category. Someone who trusts you with a heater will buy a kettle from you. Keep the buyer, widen the catalogue.


### How do I get customers to leave a review or send a photo?


Ask in the delivery-check message, when the product is new and the experience is fresh, and make it easy: "If you liked it, send me a photo I can put on my page." A parcel insert saying the same thing catches the people who do not reply to messages.


### Does repeat business work for cash-on-delivery selling?


It works particularly well. A repeat COD buyer has already paid you at the door once, so they refuse far fewer parcels than a stranger who ordered on impulse. Every customer you keep quietly lowers your return rate as well as raising your sales.
